can cause the reverse condition, a circadian rhythm longer than 24 hours, marked by difficulty waking up on time in the morning.","The suprachiasmatic nucleus regulates waking and sleeping by controlling activity levels in other brain areas, including the pineal gland (PIN-ee-al; Figure 8.7), an endocrine gland located just posterior to the thalamus.","Melatonin is a widespread chemical, found in nearly all animals—sponges are the only known exception—as well as in plants and bacteria.","People who have pineal gland tumors sometimes stay awake for days at a time. In addition to regulating sleep and wakefulness, melatonin also helps control the onset of puberty and adjustments to changes of season, such as hibernation.","Taking a melatonin pill in the evening has little effect on sleepiness because the pineal gland produces melatonin at that time anyway.","Taking melatonin earlier can hasten the onset of sleepiness and shift the circadian rhythm. Melatonin pills are sometimes helpful when people travel across time zones and need to sleep at an unaccustomed time.","Animals, including humans, have circadian rhythms— internally generated rhythms of activity and sleep lasting about 24 hours. It is difficult to adjust to a sleep schedule much different from 24 hours.","Even when people set their waking and sleeping times by the clock, the timing of sunrise influences their circadian rhythm.","It is easier for most people to follow a cycle slightly longer than 24 hours (as when traveling west) than to follow a cycle shorter than 24 hours (as when traveling east). Unlike an electric appliance that stays on until someone turns it off, the brain periodically turns itself on and off.","Our biological mechanisms prepare us to wake at certain times and sleep at other times, even if we would prefer other of Sleep and Brain Mechanisms","kind":"detailed_source_grounded_notes","printedStart":269,"printedEnd":280,"pdfStart":287,"pdfEnd":298,"content":[{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep passes through different stages, including REM sleep, while brain systems regulate wakefulness and arousal. The stages vary in brain activity and bodily responses."},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The module also describes sleep apnea, narcolepsy, REM behavior disorder, periodic limb movements, night terrors, and sleepwalking. Distinguish stages of normal sleep from conditions that interrupt or alter them."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-2-study-1","text":"Sleep has identifiable stages"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep is not one uniform state of reduced consciousness. Researchers distinguish stages through patterns of brain electrical activity, eye movements, muscle tone, and behavior. Non-REM sleep includes stages with different characteristic rhythms and depth. REM sleep, sometimes called paradoxical sleep, combines a comparatively activated brain pattern with greatly reduced skeletal muscle activity. Its distinctive physiology helps explain vivid dreams but does not mean all dreams occur only in REM."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-2-study-2","text":"Systems that promote arousal and sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Wakefulness depends on interacting brainstem, hypothalamic, and forebrain systems. Neuromodulators and local circuits help maintain alertness or encourage sleep as conditions change. Sleep involves active changes in brain regulation rather than merely switching all neurons off. Several neural processes influence transitions between wakefulness, non-REM, and REM, which is why disruption in one pathway can produce a particular type of sleep difficulty."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-2-study-3","text":"Disorders reveal mechanisms"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep apnea involves repeated interruptions of normal breathing during sleep. Narcolepsy involves unusual intrusion of sleep-related states into waking life and is linked to specialized wake-promoting mechanisms. Periodic limb movements, REM behavior disorder, night terrors, and sleepwalking differ in symptoms and sleep-stage associations. A useful comparison asks which aspect is disturbed: breathing, timing, arousal, motor inhibition, or the transition among stages."},{"type":"heading","id":"bp14-m8-2-study-4","text":"Do not confuse sleep with coma"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An unresponsive state is not automatically sleep. Sleeping people cycle through recognizable physiological stages and are typically arousable in particular ways. Other interruptions of consciousness may have different brain signatures and medical significance. Sleep stages are best understood through measurable physiology together with observed behavior, not simply whether eyes are closed."},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h01","text":"Sleep and Other Interruptions of Consciousness"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep is a state that the brain actively produces, characterized by decreased activity and decreased response to stimuli.","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In contrast, coma (KOH-muh) is an extended period of unconsciousness caused by head trauma, stroke, or disease.","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Someone in a coma has a low level of brain activity and no response to stimuli, not even to a strong pinch or a loud noise.","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people in a coma either die or begin to recover within a few weeks.","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One step up from a coma is a condition previously known as a vegetative state, now preferably called","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Breathing is more regular, and a painful stimulus increases heart rate, breathing, and sweating.","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain death is a condition with no sign of brain activity and no response to any stimulus.","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Physicians usually wait until someone has exhibited no sign of brain activity for 24 hours before pronouncing brain death, at which point most people believe it is ethical to remove life support.","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h02","text":"Stages of Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers did not even suspect that sleep has stages until they accidentally measured them, using an electroencephalograph (EEG) that records the average electrical activity near each electrode on the scalp (Figure 8.10).","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During this period, stage 1 sleep, the EEG is dominated by irregular, jagged, low-voltage waves.","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain activity is less than in relaxed wakefulness but higher than in other sleep stages.","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because most neurons are out of phase with one another, the EEG is full of short, rapid, choppy waves.","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A K-complex is a sharp wave associated with temporary inhibition of neuronal firing .","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A sleep spindle is a burst of 12- to 14-Hz waves for at least half a second.","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleep spindles result from oscillating interactions between cells in the thalamus and the cortex.","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During slow-wave sleep , heart rate, breathing rate, and brain activity decrease, while slow, large-amplitude waves increase (Figures 8.11d and e).","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h03","text":"Paradoxical or REM Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"He noticed that during certain periods of apparent sleep, the cats’ brain activity was relatively high, but their neck muscles were completely relaxed.","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After someone fell asleep, they turned the machine off, because the recording paper was expensive (before the days of computers), and they did not expect to observe anything interesting in the middle of the night anyway.","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"When they occasionally turned on the machine during the night and found evidence of eye movements, they at first assumed that something was wrong with the machine.","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They called these periods rapid eye movement (REM) sleep , and they soon realized that REM sleep was synonymous with what Jouvet called paradoxical sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers mostly use the term REM sleep , but they often prefer the term paradoxical sleep for species that lack eye movements.","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During REM sleep, the EEG shows irregular, low-voltage fast waves that indicate increased neuronal activity.","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, during REM sleep, cells in the pons and medulla inhibit movement of the postural muscles, including those that support the head.","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Later research, however, found that people awakened during non-REM sleep sometimes report dreams also.","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h04","text":"Brain Mechanisms of Wakefulness, Arousal, and Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Any animal needs to regulate its level of alertness appropriate to the situation.","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many brain areas participate in the control of sleep and wakefulness.","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h05","text":"Brain Structures of Arousal and Attention"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"After a cut through the midbrain separates the forebrain and part of the midbrain from lower structures, an animal enters prolonged sleep for the next few days.","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"We might suppose that the animal sleeps just because the cut isolated the brain from sensory stimuli.","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, if a researcher cuts each individual tract that enters the medulla and spinal cord, thus depriving the midbrain of the sensory input, the animal still has normal periods of wakefulness and sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A cut through the midbrain decreases arousal by damaging the reticular formation , a structure that extends from the medulla into the forebrain.","sourcePrintedPage":273,"sourcePdfPage":291,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some neurons of the reticular formation have axons ascending into the brain, and some have axons descending into the spinal cord.","sourcePrintedPage":273,"sourcePdfPage":291,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Magoun proposed that the reticular formation neurons with ascending axons are well suited to regulate arousal.","sourcePrintedPage":273,"sourcePdfPage":291,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Axons from some of the cells release GABA, which inhibits behavior and promotes slow-wave sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":273,"sourcePdfPage":291,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Output from the locus coeruleus increases what engineers call “gain.” It increases the activity of the most active neurons and decreases the activity of less active neurons, enhancing attention to important information .","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The hypothalamus has both neurons that promote wakefulness and neurons that promote sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Staying awake depends on orexin, especially toward the end of the day .","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Other pathways from the lateral hypothalamus regulate cells in the basal forebrain (an area just anterior and dorsal to the hypothalamus).","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h06","text":"Sleep and the Inhibition of Brain Activity"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, neurons in the thalamus become hyperpolarized, decreasing their response to stimuli and decreasing the information they send the cortex .","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The brain responds to speech, especially by an unfamiliar voice, probably because it seems more dangerous than a familiar voice .","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, neurons continue firing at only a bit less than their usual spontaneous rate.","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During sleep, axons from the pons and midbrain increase their release of GABA, inhibiting the synaptic spread of information from one neuron to another .","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Because sleep depends on GABA-mediated inhibition, sleep can be local within the brain .","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Brain areas usually wake up or go to sleep at nearly the same time, but not always.","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleepwalkers generally have their eyes open, they orient to the world enough to find their way around, and they often remember some of what they did while sleepwalking, but they are confused and vulnerable, because most of the brain is not alert enough to process information and make reasonable decisions .","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"During REM sleep, cells in the pons and medulla send messages that inhibit the spinal neurons controlling the arm and leg muscles .","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h07","text":"Sleep Disorders"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The mutant gene increases their need for sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The average adult human needs 71⁄2 to 81⁄2 hours of sleep per night, but some have been known to do well with as little as 3 hours per night .","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Researchers have found families in which several people share a mutation causing them to average less than 6 hours per night.","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most of them consider their condition an advantage, and they do not suffer memory problems or any of the other complaints people usually experience after sleep deprivation .","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It also magnifies unpleasant emotional reactions and increases the risk of depression .","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Insomnia can also be the result of epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, brain tumors, depression, anxiety, or other neurological or psychiatric conditions.","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Some children suffer insomnia because they are milk-intolerant, and their parents, not realizing the intolerance, give them milk to drink right before bedtime .","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One man suffered insomnia until he realized that he dreaded going to sleep because he hated waking up to go jogging.","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Frequent use causes dependence and an inability to sleep without the pills .","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Ordinarily that delay causes problems, although it might help combat jet lag after traveling west.","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h08","text":"Sleep Apnea"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One type of insomnia is sleep apnea , impaired ability to breathe while sleeping.","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with sleep apnea have breathless periods of a minute or so from which they awaken gasping for breath.","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They may not remember their awakenings, although they certainly notice the consequences, such as sleepiness and impaired attention the following day.","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Prolonged sleep apnea leads to a loss of neurons, with an impairment of learning and other functions .","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"People with sleep apnea are advised to lose weight and avoid alcohol and tranquilizers (which relax the breathing muscles).","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The most common treatment is a mask that covers the nose and delivers air under enough pressure to keep the breathing passages open (Figure 8.18).","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"That procedure improves sleep and blood pressure, but it only slightly decreases the risk of stroke or heart attack, probably because many people continue to be overweight .","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h09","text":"Narcolepsy"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Narcolepsy , a condition characterized by periods of sudden sleepiness during the day, affects about 1 person in 1,000.","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The H1N1 flu virus in 2009–2010 caused many cases of narcolepsy by strongly activating the immune system .","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Narcolepsy is unique among behavioral disorders as it is the only one linked to a biochemical marker (low orexin levels) that is reliable enough to establish the diagnosis.","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Using that marker is more trouble than it is worth, however, because narcolepsy is easy to identify from behavior alone.","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Mice that lack orexin and dogs that lack orexin receptors have symptoms much like human narcolepsy, with frequent alternations between wakefulness and sleep .","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Orexin itself is not an option, because it does not readily cross the blood–brain barrier, but clinical trials have begun with drugs that activate orexin receptors.","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Animal research has found that prolonged use of opiates can increase the production of orexin, even in mice engineered to develop narcolepsy .","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h10","text":"Periodic Limb Movement Disorder and REM Behavior Disorder"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Another problem is periodic limb movement disorder , characterized by repeated involuntary movement of the legs or arms during sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"syndrome, in which people often feel an urge to kick even while awake.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Many people, perhaps most, experience an occasional involuntary kick, especially when starting to fall asleep.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"In people with periodic limb movement disorder, mostly middle-aged and older, the legs kick once every 20 to 30 seconds for minutes or hours, mostly during NREM sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"However, people with REM behavior disorder move around vigorously during their REM periods, apparently acting out their dreams.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"They frequently dream about defending themselves against attack, and they may punch, kick, and leap about.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h11","text":"Night Terrors and Sleepwalking"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"A night terror is an experience of intense anxiety from which a person awakens screaming in terror.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It is more severe than a nightmare, which is simply an unpleasant dream.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Night terrors occur during NREM sleep and are more common in children than adults.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Dream content, if any, is usually simple, such as a single image.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Sleepwalking runs in families and occurs mostly in children.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Most people who sleepwalk, and many of their relatives, have additional sleep difficulties such as chronic snoring, disordered sleep breathing, bed-wetting, and night terrors .","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The causes of sleepwalking are not well understood, but it is more","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"heading","id":"deep-bp14-m8-2-h12","text":"In Closing: Stages of Sleep"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"The discovery of stages of sleep was a major landmark in psychology because researchers found a previously unrecognized distinction that is both biologically and psychologically important.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"It does not occur during REM sleep, when the large muscles are completely relaxed.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"One teenage girl walked out of her house, climbed a crane, and went back to sleep on a support beam.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evidently, some parts of the brain are awake and other parts are asleep .","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"An analogous condition is sleep sex or “sexsomnia,” in which sleeping people engage in sexual behavior, either with a partner or by masturbation, and do not remember it afterward.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"paragraph","text":"As one woman said, “After getting married a few years ago, my husband told me I was masturbating in my sleep.","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296,"sourceMethod":"selected_textbook_sentence"},{"type":"bullet","text":"Someone in this condition alternates between sleep and moderate arousal, but even during the more aroused state, the person shows no awareness of surroundings and no purposeful behavior.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287},{"type":"bullet","text":"The person might laugh or cry, but not in response to an external event.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h01","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287},{"type":"bullet","text":"Nearly every scientific advance comes from new or improved measurements.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287},{"type":"bullet","text":"The illustration shows data from a polysomnograph, a combination of EEG and eyemovement records, for a college student during various stages of sleep.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":269,"sourcePdfPage":287},{"type":"bullet","text":"As Figure 8.11c shows, the prominent characteristics of stage 2 are Kcomplexes and sleep spindles.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288},{"type":"bullet","text":"Sleep spindles increase after new learning, and the number of sleep spindles correlates positively with improvements in certain types of memory.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288},{"type":"bullet","text":"Older sources distinguished between stage 3 sleep with fewer slow waves, and stage 4 with more of them.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288},{"type":"bullet","text":"The activity is driven partly by spontaneous activity in the thalamus, and partly by waves of blood flow.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h02","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288},{"type":"bullet","text":"In the 1950s, the French scientist Michel Jouvet was trying to test the learning abilities of cats after removal of the cerebral cortex.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288},{"type":"bullet","text":"Because, as you can imagine, decorticate mammals don’t do much, Jouvet recorded slight movements of the muscles and EEGs from the hindbrain.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":270,"sourcePdfPage":288},{"type":"bullet","text":"( Paradoxical means “apparently self-contradictory.”) Meanwhile, in the United States, Nathaniel Kleitman and Eugene Aserinsky were recording eye movements to measure the onset and offset of sleep, on the assumption that eye movements stop during sleep.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289},{"type":"bullet","text":"In this regard, REM sleep is light and similar to stage 1, except for the eye movements, as illustrated in Figure 8.11f.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289},{"type":"bullet","text":"REM is also associated with erections in males and vaginal moistening in females.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289},{"type":"bullet","text":"In short, REM sleep combines aspects of deep sleep, light sleep, and features that are difficult to classify as deep or light.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":271,"sourcePdfPage":289},{"type":"bullet","text":"Shortly after the discovery of REM, researchers believed it was almost synonymous with dreaming.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h03","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290},{"type":"bullet","text":"Even after weeks of recovery, the wakeful periods are brief.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290},{"type":"bullet","text":"Evidently, the midbrain does more than just relay sensory information.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290},{"type":"bullet","text":"Those with axons descending into the spinal cord form part of the corticomedial tract of motor control.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":273,"sourcePdfPage":291},{"type":"bullet","text":"One part of the reticular formation that contributes to cortical arousal is known as the pontomesencephalon.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":273,"sourcePdfPage":291},{"type":"bullet","text":"(The term derives from pons and mesencephalon, or “midbrain.”) These neurons receive input from many sensory systems and also generate spontaneous activity, varying with the circadian rhythm.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":273,"sourcePdfPage":291},{"type":"bullet","text":"Another pathway from the hypothalamus releases a peptide neurotransmitter called either orexin or hypocretin.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292},{"type":"bullet","text":"For simplicity, this text will stick to the term orexin, but if you find the term hypocretin elsewhere, it means the same thing.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292},{"type":"bullet","text":"As a result, these cells are easily excitable, causing wakefulness.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292},{"type":"bullet","text":"REM sleep is associated with a distinctive pattern of high-amplitude electrical potentials known as PGO waves, for pons-geniculate-occipital.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":274,"sourcePdfPage":292},{"type":"bullet","text":"The stimulus to start REM sleep comes from dopamine release in the amygdala.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h05","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293},{"type":"bullet","text":"Thinking of sleep as a local phenomenon makes sense of some otherwise puzzling phenomena.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293},{"type":"bullet","text":"Enough activity occurs in the frontal and temporal cortex to enable conscious monitoring of the dreams that the rest of the brain is generating.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293},{"type":"bullet","text":"When people had lucid dreams about moving their hands, activity increased in the areas of motor cortex responsible for preparing for a hand movement— but not in the primary motor cortex that would have produced actual movements.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293},{"type":"bullet","text":"A cat with damage to those cells moves around awkwardly during REM sleep, as if it were acting out its dreams.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293},{"type":"bullet","text":"The result is temporary paralysis—a disturbing experience, if you don’t understand it.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h06","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294},{"type":"bullet","text":"Mice with one genetic mutation sleep almost four hours per day longer than other mice, and if deprived of some of that extra sleep, they react just as badly as normal mice that are deprived of part of their sleep.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294},{"type":"bullet","text":"In short, try to identify the reason for your sleep problem before you try to solve it.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294},{"type":"bullet","text":"Someone whose rhythm is phase advanced, as in Figure 8.17c, falls asleep easily but awakens early.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294},{"type":"bullet","text":"For most people, drinking coffee during the evening interferes with sleep.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h07","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294},{"type":"bullet","text":"Sleep apnea is often related to obesity, especially in middle-aged men.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h08","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294},{"type":"bullet","text":"Many men with obesity have narrower than normal airways and have to compensate by breathing frequently or vigorously.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h08","sourcePrintedPage":276,"sourcePdfPage":294},{"type":"bullet","text":"Furthermore, their airways become even narrower than usual when they adopt a sleeping posture.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h08","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295},{"type":"bullet","text":"Surgery to open the breathing spaces can be helpful in some cases, but disappointing in others.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h08","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295},{"type":"bullet","text":"It sometimes runs in families, but most cases emerge in people with no affected relatives.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295},{"type":"bullet","text":"Narcolepsy has four main symptoms, although not every patient has all four.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295},{"type":"bullet","text":"In many cases it appears to be an autoimmune reaction, in which the immune system has attacked those cells.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295},{"type":"bullet","text":"People lacking orexin alternate between short waking periods and short sleepy periods, instead of staying awake throughout the day.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h09","sourcePrintedPage":277,"sourcePdfPage":295},{"type":"bullet","text":"Leg movements are not a problem unless they become persistent.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h10","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296},{"type":"bullet","text":"For most people, the postural muscles are relaxed and inactive during REM sleep.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h10","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296},{"type":"bullet","text":"They often injure themselves or other people and damage property.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h10","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296},{"type":"bullet","text":"It also demonstrated that external measurements—in this case, EEG recordings—can be used to identify internal experiences.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h12","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296},{"type":"bullet","text":"We now take it largely for granted that an electrical or magnetic recording from the brain can tell us something about a person’s experience, but it is worth pausing to note what a surprising discovery that was in its time.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h12","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296},{"type":"bullet","text":"Sleepwalkers have been known to eat, rearrange furniture, fall off balconies, and drive cars—while disregarding lanes and traffic lights.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h12","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296},{"type":"bullet","text":"My new marriage is on the rocks, since I’m having such good sex in my sleep, I have NO desire while I’m awake.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h12","sourcePrintedPage":278,"sourcePdfPage":296},{"type":"bullet","text":"Unlike adults, infants alternate between short waking periods and short naps.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h12","sourcePrintedPage":279,"sourcePdfPage":297},{"type":"bullet","text":"After a cut through the midbrain separates the forebrain and part of the midbrain from lower structures, an animal enters prolonged sleep for the next few days.","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":272,"sourcePdfPage":290},{"type":"bullet","text":"During sleep, neurons in the thalamus become hyperpolarized, decreasing their response to stimuli and decreasing the information they send the cortex .","headingId":"bp14-m8-2-h04","sourcePrintedPage":275,"sourcePdfPage":293}],"topicIds":["bp14-m8-2-h01","bp14-m8-2-h02","bp14-m8-2-h03","bp14-m8-2-h04","bp14-m8-2-h05","bp14-m8-2-h06","bp14-m8-2-h07","bp14-m8-2-h08","bp14-m8-2-h09","bp14-m8-2-h10","bp14-m8-2-h11","bp14-m8-2-h12"],"studySections":[{"id":"bp14-m8-2-study-1","title":"Sleep has identifiable stages","text":"Sleep is not one uniform state of reduced consciousness. Researchers distinguish stages through patterns of brain electrical activity, eye movements, muscle tone, and behavior. Non-REM sleep includes stages with different characteristic rhythms and depth. REM sleep, sometimes called paradoxical sleep, combines a comparatively activated brain pattern with greatly reduced skeletal muscle activity. Its distinctive physiology helps explain vivid dreams but does not mean all dreams occur only in REM.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":269,"sourcePrintedEnd":280,"sourcePdfStart":287,"sourcePdfEnd":298},{"id":"bp14-m8-2-study-2","title":"Systems that promote arousal and sleep","text":"Wakefulness depends on interacting brainstem, hypothalamic, and forebrain systems. Neuromodulators and local circuits help maintain alertness or encourage sleep as conditions change. Sleep involves active changes in brain regulation rather than merely switching all neurons off. Several neural processes influence transitions between wakefulness, non-REM, and REM, which is why disruption in one pathway can produce a particular type of sleep difficulty.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":269,"sourcePrintedEnd":280,"sourcePdfStart":287,"sourcePdfEnd":298},{"id":"bp14-m8-2-study-3","title":"Disorders reveal mechanisms","text":"Sleep apnea involves repeated interruptions of normal breathing during sleep. Narcolepsy involves unusual intrusion of sleep-related states into waking life and is linked to specialized wake-promoting mechanisms. Periodic limb movements, REM behavior disorder, night terrors, and sleepwalking differ in symptoms and sleep-stage associations. A useful comparison asks which aspect is disturbed: breathing, timing, arousal, motor inhibition, or the transition among stages.","kind":"companion_original_explanation","sourcePrintedStart":269,"sourcePrintedEnd":280,"sourcePdfStart":287,"sourcePdfEnd":298},{"id":"bp14-m8-2-study-4","title":"Do not confuse sleep with coma","text":"An unresponsive state is not automatically sleep. Sleeping people cycle through recognizable physiological stages and are typically arousable in particular ways. Other interruptions of consciousness may have different brain signatures and medical significance. (Figure 8.10).","printedPage":269,"pdfPage":287,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":20},{"text":"During this period, stage 1 sleep, the EEG is dominated oscillating interactions between cells in the thalamus and the e).","printedPage":270,"pdfPage":288,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":27}],"sourceWordCount":384},{"id":"bp14-m8-2-h03","title":"Paradoxical or REM do much, Jouvet recorded slight movements of the muscles and EEGs from the self-contradictory.”) Meanwhile, in the United States, Nathaniel Kleitman and Eugene Aserinsky were recording eye movements to measure the onset and offset of sleep, on the assumption that eye movements stop during sleep.","printedPage":271,"pdfPage":289,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":120},{"text":"In this regard, REM sleep is light and similar to stage 1, except for the eye movements, as illustrated in Figure 8.11f.","printedPage":271,"pdfPage":289,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":121},{"text":"REM is also associated with erections in males and vaginal moistening in females.","printedPage":271,"pdfPage":289,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":122},{"text":"In short, REM sleep combines aspects of deep sleep, light sleep, and features that are difficult to classify as deep or light.","printedPage":271,"pdfPage":289,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":123},{"text":"Shortly after the discovery of REM, researchers believed it was almost synonymous with .","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"subsection_source_overview","paragraphIndex":161,"sourceTopicId":"bp14-m8-2-h06"}],"originalFacts":2,"additionalFacts":0,"glossary":[],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":24,"sourceStatus":"parent_overview_from_verified_subsections","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":73,"overviewSource":"Study-point Attention","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m8-2-h04","printedPage":272,"pdfPage":290,"facts":[{"text":"After a cut through the midbrain separates the forebrain and part of the midbrain from lower structures, an animal enters prolonged sleep for the next few days.","printedPage":272,"pdfPage":290,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":41},{"text":"We might suppose that the animal sleeps just because the cut isolated the brain from sensory stimuli.","printedPage":272,"pdfPage":290,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":42},{"text":"However, if a researcher cuts each individual tract that enters the medulla and spinal cord, thus depriving the midbrain of the sensory input, the animal still has normal periods of wakefulness and sleep.","printedPage":272,"pdfPage":290,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":43},{"text":"A cut through the midbrain decreases arousal by damaging the reticular formation , a structure that extends from the medulla into the forebrain.","printedPage":273,"pdfPage":291,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":44},{"text":"Some neurons of the reticular formation have axons ascending into the brain, and some have axons descending into the spinal cord.","printedPage":273,"pdfPage":291,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":45},{"text":"Magoun proposed that the reticular formation neurons with ascending axons are well suited to regulate arousal.","printedPage":273,"pdfPage":291,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":46},{"text":"Axons from some of the cells release GABA, which inhibits behavior and promotes slow-wave sleep .","printedPage":273,"pdfPage":291,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":47},{"text":"Output from the locus coeruleus increases what engineers call “gain.” It increases the activity of the most active neurons and decreases the activity of less active neurons, enhancing attention to important information .","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":48},{"text":"The hypothalamus has both neurons that promote wakefulness and neurons that promote sleep .","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":49},{"text":"Staying awake depends on orexin, especially toward the end of the day .","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":50},{"text":"Other pathways from the lateral hypothalamus regulate cells in the basal forebrain (an area just anterior and dorsal to the hypothalamus).","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":51},{"text":"Even after weeks of recovery, the wakeful periods are brief.","printedPage":272,"pdfPage":290,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":125},{"text":"Evidently, the midbrain does more than just relay sensory information.","printedPage":272,"pdfPage":290,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":126},{"text":"Those with axons descending into the spinal cord form part of the corticomedial tract of motor control.","printedPage":273,"pdfPage":291,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":127},{"text":"One part of the reticular formation that contributes to cortical arousal is known as the pontomesencephalon.","printedPage":273,"pdfPage":291,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":128},{"text":"(The term derives from pons and mesencephalon, or “midbrain.”) These neurons receive input from many sensory systems and also generate spontaneous activity, varying with the circadian rhythm.","printedPage":273,"pdfPage":291,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":129},{"text":"Another pathway from the hypothalamus releases a peptide neurotransmitter called either orexin or hypocretin.","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":130},{"text":"For simplicity, this text will stick to the term orexin, but if you find the term hypocretin elsewhere, it means the same thing.","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":131},{"text":"As a result, these cells are easily excitable, causing wakefulness.","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":132},{"text":"REM sleep is associated with a distinctive pattern of high-amplitude electrical potentials known as PGO waves, for pons-geniculate-occipital.","printedPage":274,"pdfPage":292,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":133},{"text":"The stimulus to start REM sleep comes from dopamine release in the amygdala.","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":134}],"originalFacts":11,"additionalFacts":10,"glossary":[{"term":"Lateral hypothalamus","definition":"area of the hypothalamus that controls insulin secretion, alters taste responsiveness, and facilitates feeding in other ways","sourcePrintedPage":626,"sourcePdfPage":644},{"term":"Reticular formation","definition":"a structure that extends from the medulla into the forebrain; controls motor areas of the spinal cord and selectively increases arousal and attention in various forebrain areas","sourcePrintedPage":631,"sourcePdfPage":649},{"term":"Basal forebrain","definition":"area anterior and dorsal to the hypothalamus; includes cell clusters","sourcePrintedPage":619,"sourcePdfPage":637},{"term":"Locus coeruleus","definition":"a small structure in the pons that emits bursts of impulses in response to meaningful events, especially those that produce emotional arousal","sourcePrintedPage":626,"sourcePdfPage":644},{"term":"PGO waves","definition":"a distinctive pattern of highamplitude electrical potentials","sourcePrintedPage":629,"sourcePdfPage":647}],"sourceBodyWordsAvailable":907,"sourceStatus":"source_explained","mdCrosscheck":"terms_present","wordCount":392},{"id":"bp14-m8-2-h06","title":"Sleep and the Inhibition of Brain Activity","level":2,"parentId":"bp14-m8-2-h04","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"facts":[{"text":"During sleep, neurons in the thalamus become hyperpolarized, decreasing their response to stimuli and decreasing the information they send the cortex .","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":53},{"text":"The brain responds to speech, especially by an unfamiliar voice, probably because it seems more dangerous than a familiar voice .","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":54},{"text":"During sleep, neurons continue firing at only a bit less than their usual spontaneous rate.","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":55},{"text":"During sleep, axons from the pons and midbrain increase their release of GABA, inhibiting the synaptic spread of information from one neuron to another .","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":56},{"text":"Because sleep depends on GABA-mediated inhibition, sleep can be local within the brain .","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":57},{"text":"Brain areas usually wake up or go to sleep at nearly the same time, but not always.","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":58},{"text":"Sleepwalkers generally have their eyes open, they orient to the world enough to find their way around, and they often remember some of what they did while sleepwalking, but they are confused and vulnerable, because most of the brain is not alert enough to process information and make reasonable decisions .","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":59},{"text":"During REM sleep, cells in the pons and medulla send messages that inhibit the spinal neurons controlling the arm and leg muscles .","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":60},{"text":"Thinking of sleep as a local phenomenon makes sense of some otherwise puzzling phenomena.","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":135},{"text":"Enough activity occurs in the frontal and temporal cortex to enable conscious monitoring of the dreams that the rest of the brain is generating.","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":136},{"text":"When people had lucid dreams about moving their hands, activity increased in the areas of motor cortex responsible for preparing for a hand movement— but not in the primary motor cortex that would have produced actual movements.","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":137},{"text":"A cat with damage to those cells moves around awkwardly during REM sleep, as if it were acting out its dreams.","printedPage":275,"pdfPage":293,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":138},{"text":"The result is temporary paralysis—a disturbing experience, if you don’t understand it.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":139}],"originalFacts":8,"additionalFacts":5,"glossary":[{"term":"Primary .","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":62},{"text":"The average adult human needs 71⁄2 to 81⁄2 hours of sleep per night, but some have been known to do well with as little as 3 hours per night .","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":63},{"text":"Researchers have found families in which several people share a mutation causing them to average less than 6 hours per night.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":64},{"text":"Most of them consider their condition an advantage, and they do not suffer memory problems or any of the other complaints people usually experience after sleep deprivation .","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":65},{"text":"It also magnifies unpleasant emotional reactions and increases the risk of depression .","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":66},{"text":"Insomnia can also be the result of epilepsy, Parkinson’s disease, brain tumors, depression, anxiety, or other neurological or psychiatric conditions.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":67},{"text":"Some children suffer insomnia because they are milk-intolerant, and their parents, not realizing the intolerance, give them milk to drink right before bedtime .","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":68},{"text":"One man suffered insomnia until he realized that he dreaded going to sleep because he hated waking up to go jogging.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":69},{"text":"Frequent use causes dependence and an inability to sleep without the pills .","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":70},{"text":"Ordinarily that delay causes problems, although it might help combat jet lag after traveling west.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":71},{"text":"Mice with one genetic mutation sleep almost four hours per day longer than other mice, and if deprived of some of that extra sleep, they react just as badly as normal mice that are deprived of part of their sleep.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":140},{"text":"In short, try to identify the reason for your sleep problem before you try to solve it.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":141},{"text":"Someone whose rhythm is phase advanced, as in Figure 8.17c, falls asleep easily but awakens early.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":142},{"text":"For most people, drinking coffee during the evening interferes with or so from which they awaken gasping for breath.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":74},{"text":"They may not remember their awakenings, although they certainly notice the consequences, such as sleepiness and impaired attention the following day.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":75},{"text":"Prolonged sleep apnea leads to a loss of neurons, with an impairment of learning and other functions .","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":76},{"text":"People with sleep apnea are advised to lose weight and avoid alcohol and tranquilizers (which relax the breathing muscles).","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":77},{"text":"The most common treatment is a mask that covers the nose and delivers air under enough pressure to keep the breathing passages open (Figure 8.18).","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":78},{"text":"That procedure improves sleep and blood pressure, but it only slightly decreases the risk of stroke or heart attack, probably because many people continue to be overweight .","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":79},{"text":"Sleep apnea is often related to obesity, especially in middle-aged men.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":144},{"text":"Many men with obesity have narrower than normal airways and have to compensate by breathing frequently or vigorously.","printedPage":276,"pdfPage":294,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":145},{"text":"Furthermore, their airways become even narrower than usual when they adopt a sleeping posture.","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":146},{"text":"Surgery to open the breathing spaces can be helpful in some cases, but disappointing in diagnosis.","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":83},{"text":"Using that marker is more trouble than it is worth, .","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":85},{"text":"Orexin itself is not an option, because it does not readily cross increase the production of orexin, even in mice engineered to develop narcolepsy .","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":87},{"text":"It sometimes runs in families, but most cases emerge in people with no affected relatives.","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":148},{"text":"Narcolepsy has four main symptoms, although not every patient has all four.","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":149},{"text":"In many cases it appears to be an autoimmune reaction, in which the immune system has attacked those cells.","printedPage":277,"pdfPage":295,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"additional_source_condensed_note","paragraphIndex":150},{"text":"People lacking orexin alternate between short waking periods and short sleepy periods, instead of staying awake throughout the usually simple, such as a single image.","printedPage":278,"pdfPage":296,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":99},{"text":"Sleepwalking runs in families .","printedPage":278,"pdfPage":296,"source":"user_uploaded_pdf","method":"selected_textbook_sentence","paragraphIndex":101},{"text":"The causes of sleepwalking are not well understood, but it is Physicians usually wait until someone has exhibited no sign of brain activity for 24 hours before pronouncing brain death, at which point most people believe it is ethical to remove life support.","Researchers did not even suspect that sleep has stages until they accidentally measured them, using an electroencephalograph (EEG) that records the average electrical activity near each electrode on the scalp (Figure 8.10).","During this period, stage 1 sleep, the EEG is dominated by irregular, jagged, low-voltage waves.","Brain activity is less than in relaxed wakefulness but higher than in other sleep stages. Because most neurons are out of phase with one another, the EEG is full of short, rapid, choppy waves.","A K-complex is a sharp wave associated with temporary inhibition of neuronal firing.","A sleep spindle is a burst of 12- to 14-Hz waves for at least half a second.","Sleep spindles result from oscillating interactions between cells in the thalamus and the cortex.
